entries.basis: Explicit NONBLIND source/anchor adjudication after saving toub-third-34.json; this is not a fourth independent vote. Preserve originals32-verify level4/violin3/medium, originals32-blind level2/violin1/medium, and toub-third-34 level3/violin3/medium. The supported band is 2–4. Choose 3 from technical evidence, not averaging: the full score shows violin3 changing at V (m249, p16) to a repeated low E4-to-A5 leap followed by G5-F5-E5-D5-C5, with comparable register changes later exchanged among inner/lower parts. These repeated shifts/string transfers at sixteenth=384/min and the sustained nine-minute texture warrant upper-intermediate control beyond grading only the low first-violin scale. The level2 review correctly identifies moderate tempo, simple rhythm and lack of double stops/specialist bowing but overweights violin1 duration when naming the hardest part; sampled compact register does not dispose of the recurring A5 leap. The level4 review correctly selects violin3 and recognizes stamina/register changes, but its broad upper-register/endurance account does not identify the extra advanced technical vocabulary normally needed to distinguish early advanced from upper intermediate. A5 is manageable with ordinary intermediate position work; patterns are strongly repetitive, mostly scalar, in unchanged 2/4 and treble clef, with no rapid mixed rhythms, chords, double stops or prescribed virtuoso bow strokes. Late accidental changes increase finger-pattern vigilance but do not create a new higher register or speed tier. Thus 3 is a supported central technical placement with adjacent-level uncertainty; retain medium advisory confidence without upgrade. No ensemble-count uplift, no professional-performer grade inference. Source/date facts already verified remain preserved: do not resolve 2017 score/title versus 2012 album metadata or infer a live quartet from the stated human multitrack.
